name: WebP Converter & Image Optimizer
author: SPINX Digital

sections.description:
Reduce image file sizes and optimize your WordPress Media Library with WebP Converter & Image Optimizer. Convert JPEG, PNG, and GIF images to WebP directly on your server using PHP’s GD or ImageMagick extension.

Automatically convert supported uploads, bulk-convert existing media, process WordPress thumbnail sizes, and restore original images when needed. No external image optimization service, API account, or monthly conversion quota is required.

Key Features

Local WebP Conversion
Convert supported JPEG, PNG, and GIF images to WebP using your server’s available PHP image processing extension. Your image files do not need to be uploaded to an external optimization service.

Automatic Image Conversion
Automatically generate WebP versions of supported images when they are uploaded to WordPress.

Bulk Media Library Conversion
Process existing Media Library images in manageable batches. Track conversion progress and identify successful, pending, and failed conversions.

WordPress Thumbnail Support
Generate WebP versions of original images and WordPress-generated thumbnail sizes.

Privacy-Focused Processing
Image conversion runs locally on your server without sending image files to a third-party optimization service.

No Monthly Conversion Limits
Convert images without monthly quotas or per-image API charges. Actual processing capacity depends on your server resources and configuration.

Consistent WebP Quality
The free version uses a fixed WebP quality setting of 75 for image conversion.

Restore Original Images
Restore original images and remove generated WebP files individually or in bulk.

Conversion Dashboard
Monitor converted, pending, failed, and previously processed images. View reported storage savings from your image optimization activity.

Media Library Integration
Convert or restore individual images using the plugin’s Media Library actions and attachment controls.

Protected REST API
Access supported statistics, health checks, logs, settings, exports, and image management actions through protected REST API endpoints.

Why Choose WebP Converter & Image Optimizer?

WebP Converter & Image Optimizer helps WordPress website owners manage image optimization without depending on cloud-based conversion services.

Whether you run a blog, business website, portfolio, or eCommerce store, the plugin provides tools to convert images in bulk, automate conversion for new uploads, track processing results, and restore original files when needed.

By generating WebP versions, the plugin can help reduce image file sizes and support better website performance. Actual savings depend on the original images, conversion settings, and server configuration.

Key benefits:

  • Convert supported images directly on your server.
  • Automate conversion for new uploads.
  • Bulk-process existing Media Library images.
  • Generate WebP versions of WordPress thumbnails.
  • Monitor conversion status and reported storage savings.
  • Restore original images when required.
  • Convert images without monthly quotas or external API charges.

WebP Converter & Image Optimizer Pro

The free version includes local WebP conversion, automatic upload conversion, bulk processing, thumbnail support, conversion tracking, and restoration.

The optional Pro add-on provides additional controls and advanced image management features.

Pro features include:

  • Custom WebP quality settings and image format filters.
  • Detailed system logs and conversion error information.
  • Post content URL replacement tools.
  • Advanced image management.
  • Before-and-after image comparison.
  • Pause and resume controls for bulk conversion and restoration.
  • WP Offload Media compatibility with supported cloud storage and CDN workflows.
  • Controlled SVG uploads, sanitization, and Media Library previews.
  • Large image scaling controls.

Explore the Pro add-on: https://apps.spinxdigital.com/

Get Started

Install WebP Converter & Image Optimizer to convert supported images to WebP, process your existing Media Library, and manage original files directly from your WordPress dashboard.

Start optimizing your WordPress images with local processing, flexible workflows, and no monthly conversion quotas.
sections.installation:
WordPress Admin Method

  1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New.
  2. Search for WebP Converter & Image Optimizer.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  4. Open WebP Optimizer from the WordPress admin menu.

FTP Method

  1. Upload the spinx-digital-image-converter folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Open WebP Optimizer from the WordPress admin menu.

After Activation

  1. Review the conversion engine (GD or ImageMagick) and delivery settings.
  2. Run Bulk Convert to process existing images, or leave auto-convert enabled to handle new uploads automatically.
sections.faq:
Which image formats can the plugin convert?

The plugin supports JPEG, PNG, and GIF to WebP conversion, subject to the capabilities of your server’s image processing extension.

Does the plugin convert WordPress thumbnails?

Yes. The plugin can generate WebP versions of original images and WordPress-generated thumbnail sizes.

Are my images uploaded to an external service?

No. Image conversion is performed locally on your server without sending image files to an external optimization service.

Can images be converted automatically when uploaded?

Yes. The plugin can automatically generate WebP versions of supported images when they are uploaded to WordPress.

How does bulk conversion work?

The plugin processes existing Media Library images in batches and displays conversion progress in the dashboard.

Can I restore my original images?

Yes. You can restore original images and remove generated WebP files individually or in bulk.

Does the plugin support GD and ImageMagick?

Yes. It supports PHP’s GD and ImageMagick extensions, depending on server availability and configuration.

Does the free version have conversion limits?

There are no monthly conversion quotas. The number and size of images you can process depend on your server resources and configuration.

Is a Pro version available?

Yes. The optional Pro add-on includes advanced conversion settings, image comparison, additional management tools, supported cloud-storage workflows, and SVG-related features.

Where can I get support?

Visit the plugin’s Support section on WordPress.org to ask questions, report issues, or get help with the plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4

  • Improved: Media Library screens load much faster on sites that offload media to cloud storage (Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, and similar). The plugin no longer checks remote storage paths when looking for local WebP files, which previously added a network request for every image shown.
  • Improved: WebP image dimensions are now read from the file header instead of loading the whole image into memory, lowering memory use when displaying WebP details.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.1.

1.0.3

  • New: optional server-level WebP delivery. Choose “Server rewrite (.htaccess)” in Settings to serve WebP files on the original image URL via rewrite rules in uploads/.htaccess (Apache/LiteSpeed), with automatic fallback to the original image for browsers without WebP support.
  • The server rewrite mode covers images referenced anywhere — page builders, theme templates, CSS — and keeps serving WebP even while the plugin is deactivated. The rules are removed when the plugin is deleted or the delivery method is switched back.
  • Restoring an image works exactly as before: the WebP file is deleted and the server automatically serves the original again. No content or database URLs are modified by this delivery mode.
  • Default behavior is unchanged: the existing PHP filter delivery remains the default.

1.0.2

  • Performance improvement change.

1.0.1

  • Plugin URI updated to the official WordPress.org plugin page.
  • Improved plugin architecture, portability, security, and performance.
  • Quality setting sanitization and native persistence improvements.
  • Removed the previous per-image conversion size limitation.
  • Improved file path handling and upload directory compatibility.
  • Optimized bulk conversion batch processing and registration.
  • Removed unused legacy AJAX endpoints and obsolete admin assets.
  • Removed PHP error-suppression operators from runtime code.
  • Added support for image-type conversion controls (JPEG, PNG, and GIF).
  • Added support for pause and resume functionality during bulk conversion processes.
  • Added smart bulk action controls with automatic button state management.
  • Improved pending image count accuracy based on enabled image types.
  • Added dashboard drill-down integration support for companion add-ons.
  • Improved dashboard statistics accuracy.
  • Add 75% fixed quality conversion.
  • Fixed duplicate WebP thumbnail generation and improved thumbnail reuse.
  • Added automatic cleanup of legacy duplicate WebP thumbnails.
  • Fixed restore operations to remove all generated WebP files and orphaned conversion data.
  • Improved image restoration reliability and cleanup processes.
  • Enhanced Images screen responsiveness for mobile and tablet devices.
  • Improved image management interface with touch-friendly action buttons and responsive layouts.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Automatic WebP conversion for new uploads (JPEG, PNG, GIF).
  • Bulk conversion for existing Media Library images with batch processing.
  • Dashboard with converted, pending, failed, and storage-saved statistics.
  • Media Library row actions for per-image convert and restore.
  • GD and ImageMagick engine support with automatic detection.
  • REST endpoints for stats, health checks, settings, exports, and image actions.
  • Unified bulk job status model with bulk status endpoint.
